title: The project list grew in several directions
summary:
More people brought things to build with, while the APIs got easier to explore and more predictable to use.

The community listings gained Persian-language chat, browser and desktop image generators, an Arabic coding-education platform, and projects spanning agents, diagrams, travel, messaging, and collaborative art. October contribution guidelines also clarified which merged PRs count toward the event badge.

Enter added an image-model listing endpoint and an API reference for generation requests. The image API now gives more useful reasons when Nano Banana produces no image, and model response headers use registry names rather than internal provider paths. The guide also gained reference-image and sizing details. Seedream now requires Flower access, and Kontext was removed from the available image models.

Account management became less fussy: API keys no longer require an allowed-domains field, deletion asks for confirmation, and the profile menu links to the customer portal. The account page shows Pollen balances to four decimal places, while signup handles existing Polar customer records. The new API reference and broader request validation make generation requests easier to put together.

Cache exclusions were narrowed to exact paths, HEAD requests now reuse GET cache entries without returning a body, and text-cache entries carry less metadata. POST requests to the text API root can also use cached responses. Together, these changes remove several ways a reusable response could miss the cache.
